title: Pseudo-Dionysius and Maximus Confessor Scholia
shelf_note: A Greek minuscule manuscript of the Celestial Hierarchy (ch. 15, the angels' garments and instruments) with scholia in the margin in majuscule. That matches the title. There is no tradition or collection to check it against.
rights_flag: The Vatican Library's copyright banner is burned into the scan, "Copyright © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana / powered by AMLAD·NTT DATA", and a diagonal watermark "Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana ... ALL RIGHTS RESERVED" runs across the text block. The work itself is medieval. This flag is about the licence on the digitisation.
structure_note: The book has 390 records, and all 390 have OCR. But structure.pages_translated is 0 while the book field says 378. One of those two counters is wrong. In a manuscript with no printed pagination, 47 backsteps and 38 repeats among 183 'printed' numbers probably come from the OCR taking marginal chapter numerals (e.g. ις') or folio marks as page numbers. That is a counting artefact, not a splice.

pages.layout: single column of minuscule text with enlarged initials in the left margin; majuscule scholia in the left margin, keyed by † and ※ signs, and below the text block; a strip of the facing leaf at the right edge (correctly ignored by the OCR)

ocr_errors.image: The paragraph opens with an enlarged Ἀ: "Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ αὖθις ἡ … σοφία · καὶ τοὺς … ἀμφιέννυσι … δίδωσι περιφέρειν αὐτοῖς · φέρε καὶ τὰ τῶν οὐρανίων νόων ἱερὰ … καὶ ὄργανα". The image has 'since … wisdom clothes them and gives them [things] to carry; come, let us unfold the sacred [garments] and instruments of the heavenly minds'. It does not have 'established in the gods' or 'the gifts of the gods'.
ocr_errors.problem: The sentence is rebuilt into one that is not on the leaf. The heavenly 'minds' (νόων) become 'gods', and the exhortation φέρε … ἀναπτύξωμεν becomes a statement

tr_errors.source:
Ἡ μὲν ἀληθινὴ καὶ ἁπλῆ καὶ μονοειδὴς σοφία.
ἐν τοῖς θεοῖς ἵδρυται
tr_errors.english: The true, simple and uniform **wisdom** <note>original: σοφία (sophia)</note> is established in the gods; and it clothes them with the encircling garment that bestows honours upon them. It bears the gifts of the gods in heavenly forms and instruments.
tr_errors.problem: This faithfully renders an OCR sentence that is not on the leaf (see the O1 error above). The reader gets a doctrine about 'the gods' where the manuscript is about the heavenly minds, plus the exhortation 'let us unfold'

tr_errors.source:
καὶ τὸ καθόλου νοητῶς ἐκλάμπον. ἡμᾶς
δὲ ἐκλαμπόμενον
tr_errors.english: and that which shines forth wholly in an **intelligible** manner, yet is itself illuminated toward us
tr_errors.problem: The image reads 'or is intellectually (νοερῶς) illuminated'. The English loses the intelligible/intellectual pair that the scholion beside it explains, so the scholion no longer connects to the text

tr_errors.source: τὰ δὲ ὄργανα. καὶ τοὺς πέλεκεις.
tr_errors.problem: The manuscript reads δόρατα, 'spears'. The note certifies the misread as the original word

other.note: Invented markdown bold (**wisdom**, **garment**, **rods** …) runs through the reader text

missing.english: Where it is, in the 16th reading, in the seventh chapter.
missing.why: An opaque cross-reference. The reader is not told which work or which 'reading' the scholiast means
The Celestial Hierarchy has 15 chapters, so the reference must point to another work. The reader needs to be told which

missing.english: In the work On the Divine Names, in chapter 4, he also spoke about light.
missing.why: The reader needs to know that On the Divine Names is another treatise by the same Pseudo-Dionysius, and that this marginal text is a scholion (attributed to Maximus) on the main text

book_verdict: The page is the correct leaf, and its OCR follows the general argument. But at several points it rebuilds the minuscule into plausible Greek that is not on the leaf ('established in the gods', 'instruments' for spears, 'us' for νοερῶς), and the English and its notes pass those readings on as fact. A Vatican copyright banner and watermark are burned into the scan.
